intro: Ir a + infinitive: the easiest way to talk about your plans.
p.voy.consejo: «Voy» is the yo form of «ir» in the present. It is written with v but sounds like b.
p.vas.consejo: «Vas» is for «tú». With he or she you say «va».
p.va.consejo: «Va» has no h. «Ha» with h is another verb (haber).
p.vamos.consejo: «Vamos a + infinitive» also invites others to do something together: «¡Vamos a comer!».
p.vais.consejo: «Vais» is mainly used in Spain. In Latin America people say «ustedes van».
p.van.consejo: «Van» works for they and ustedes. Only «ir» changes: «van a comer».
p.a.glosa: small word that links «ir» to the verb of the plan
p.a.consejo: In «voy a viajar» the «a» is never missing: without it the sentence sounds incomplete.
p.viajar.consejo: It is written with v and j, but sounds «bya-HAR», with j like a strong h.
p.hacer.consejo: After «ir a» the second verb never changes: «voy a hacer», «vamos a hacer».
p.mañana.consejo: It also means the first part of the day: «por la mañana». The context shows which one.
p.el próximo.consejo: It changes with the noun: «el próximo mes», «la próxima semana», «los próximos días».
p.el mes.consejo: It is masculine: «el mes», «un mes». The plural is «los meses».
p.llover.consejo: It is only used in the singular: «va a llover». The ll sounds like y.
b1.texto:
To talk about a plan, use **ir a + infinitive**:

- **Voy a** viajar.
- **Vas a** estudiar.
- **Vamos a** comer.

Only the verb **ir** changes: **voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van**. The second verb **never changes**: it always stays in the infinitive.
b2.f0.texto: What are you going to do tomorrow?
b2.f1.texto: I'm going to travel to Granada.
b2.f2.texto: What are your parents going to do?
b2.f3.texto: They are going to eat in the countryside.
b2.f5.texto: Next month it is going to rain little.
b2.f6.texto: Then I'm going to travel with you.
b4.titulo: Ir in the present + a + infinitive
b4.texto:
The verb **ir** is irregular:

- yo **voy**
- tú **vas**
- he, she, usted **va**
- we **vamos**
- you plural (vosotros) **vais**
- they, ustedes **van**

After it always comes **a** and an **infinitive**: **voy a comer**, **van a viajar**. With **llover** and other weather verbs there is no subject: **va a llover**.
b4.e0.texto: We are going to eat at two.
b4.e1.texto: Tomorrow you are going to travel.
b4.e2.texto: My friend is going to make a cake.
b5.f0.texto: Tomorrow I am going to travel to Granada on a blue train.
b5.f1.texto: The suitcase waits open beside the window.
b5.f2.texto: I am going to pack a soft scarf and an old book.
b5.f3.texto: The sun is going to rise slowly over the roofs.
b5.f4.texto: My heart is going to beat fast on the platform.
b5.f5.texto: My cousin is going to wait for me at the station with a colourful sign.
b5.f6.texto: The narrow streets are going to smell of warm bread.
b5.f7.texto: We are going to climb slowly up to the hill of the neighbourhood.
b5.f8.texto: The white houses are going to shine under the golden light.
b5.f9.texto: At the end of the day I am going to sleep with a calm smile.
b6.o2.refuerzo: After «a» comes the infinitive, not the participle.
b6.pregunta: You want to tell a plan. Which sentence is right?
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Vamos» is for «nosotros»; here only you speak.
b8.frase: Mañana voy a viajar a Granada
b8.traduccion: Tomorrow I am going to travel to Granada
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Comer» stays in the infinitive; it does not change.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! Only «ir» changes: voy, vas, va, vamos…
b9.o2.refuerzo: Only one changes: the second verb stays the same.
b9.pregunta: In «Vamos a comer», which verb changes with the person?
b10.frase: Mis padres ____ a comer en el campo.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Va» is for one person; «mis padres» are several.
b10.pregunta: Which form of «ir» goes with «mis padres»?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I'm going to study tomorrow».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Voy» is yo: you ask about yourself, not your friend.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Perfect! «Vas» is tú and «hacer» stays in the infinitive.
b12.pregunta: You ask a friend about his plan. What do you say?
p.amiga.consejo: «Amiga» is feminine; for a boy it is «amigo». The g is hard: a-MI-ga.
p.guardar.consejo: It also means «to keep» and «to save»: «guardar un secreto». The u is silent only in «gue/gui».
p.bufanda.consejo: You wear it around the neck when it is cold. It is feminine: «una bufanda».
p.latir.consejo: It says what the heart does: «el corazón late». It is a regular -ir verb.
p.prima.consejo: The male cousin is «primo». «Primos» can mean cousins of both sexes.
p.colina.consejo: It is smaller than a «montaña». The stress is on «li»: ko-LI-na.
p.casas.consejo: It is the plural of «casa»: add -s. The c before a sounds like k.
